clue.text: On entrance, block attempt to get interview

definitions.meaning: the slab or step of stone laid at the threshold of a house, a block on an entrance
as a verb, of reporters who wait at someone's front door to buttonhole them for a story

explanation.surface: A journalist stands at the entrance, blocking the way in an effort to secure an interview.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is the step before a front door; the verb is the press tactic of ambushing a subject at home for quotes.

clue.text: Passes targets in performances with ball and bat

parts.note: in cricket an over is a spell of six balls bowled by one bowler
runs are what a batsman scores with the bat in cricket

explanation.surface: A cricketer's performances with ball and bat exceed his aims.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: an OVER is six balls bowled; RUNS are scored with the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: To go beyond set limits or targets, as a project does with its budget, is to exceed them.

clue.text: He painted bottom drawer without opening it

indicators.note: losing the opening letter, so the first letter of the word for bottom drawer goes

parts.note: a bottom drawer is British for a bride's collection of linen and clothes, a trousseau

explanation.surface: Someone paints the lowest drawer of a chest without ever opening it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without opening' drops the T from TROUSSEAU. A bottom drawer is the British term for a bride-to-be's store of household linen.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri, the French naive painter of jungle scenes, is a man who painted.

clue.text: Fabric sample that's used for making up

parts.note: toile is a light linen or cotton fabric
to sample something is to try it, a try

explanation.surface: A swatch of fabric that a dressmaker uses for making up garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making up' suggests sewing, but means putting on make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmetics and washing articles count as toiletries, articles used in grooming and putting on make-up.

clue.text: Individual unnamed, traitor held by state — one in disgrace

parts.note: a person is an individual
anon, short for anonymous, means unnamed

indicators.note: kept inside, so one piece sits within another

parts.note: GA is the abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
a rat is a traitor or informer

explanation.surface: An anonymous traitor is detained by the state and disgraced.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase for an unwelcome person, typically a diplomat expelled, describes someone out of favour.

clue.text: Standard guide offering academic choice

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, in favour of, the word an offering is made for
picking form A, a class at school, is an academic choice

explanation.surface: A standard guidebook lists the academic options on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: A FORM is a school class in Britain, so choosing form A is an academic choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma is a standard document or template, a fixed form to follow.

clue.text: Mother picked up excellent line in Fabric

parts.note: mater is Latin, and old British schoolboy slang, for mother

indicators.note: lifted, so in a down entry the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, excellent, the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A mother lifts a fine thread from a piece of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' turns A1 (with 1 as I) upwards in this down clue to give IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloth or textile is material, the stuff garments are made from.

clue.text: Made to go round with it, start to make delivery

indicators.note: around, so the first word goes about the others

parts.note: someone who was made to go was sent
it, meaning fashionable, is hip

indicators.note: the start of the word make, its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone forced to circle round with something starts to make a delivery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' is the old slang sense of fashionable, hip; 'round' is the container signal and 'start to' takes M from make.
explanation.definitionFit: A consignment of goods sent out is a delivery.

clue.text: Trespass, fence being extremely deficient, to fish

indicators.note: lacking at the extremes, so the word fence loses its first and last letters

parts.note: a roach is a freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks onto private land through a gap at the ends of a fence to go fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being extremely deficient' strips the first and last letters from FENCE, leaving ENC.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude on land or rights belonging to another is to trespass.

clue.text: Special British and European coins taken by cheat

parts.note: P stands for pence, British coins
the ecu was the European currency unit, the forerunner of the euro
a liar is a deceiver, one who cheats with untruths

explanation.surface: A swindler pockets a mix of pounds and continental money.
explanation.walkthrough: The one phrase gives two coins: P for British pence and ECU for the old European unit; 'taken by' puts the cheat after them.
explanation.definitionFit: Something particular to one person or thing is special to it, as in a quality peculiar to cats.

clue.text: Sort of book with chances of promotion to number one

parts.note: number one is slang for oneself, as in looking after number one
help, a leg-up, is what gives someone the chance of advancement

explanation.surface: A book offering a way to get ahead at work and look after yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as help given to oneself: chances of advancement offered to number one, oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuals for personal improvement form a whole publishing genre named after helping yourself.

clue.text: Stage magician to get on must join circle

parts.note: to get on in life is to prosper or thrive
O is the shape of a circle

explanation.surface: A theatrical conjuror who wants to succeed must join the Magic Circle.
explanation.walkthrough: The Magic Circle is the famous British society of conjurors, which colours the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The exiled sorcerer of Shakespeare's The Tempest is literally a magician on the stage.

clue.text: Coach's left mean team

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy or tight-fisted
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A football coach complains that his team is stingy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' looks like a sports trainer, but it is a vehicle: in Britain the near side of a vehicle is the left, by the kerb.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage the kerbside of a road vehicle, the left-hand side, is called by this term.

clue.text: Like Holmes's face, if he'd failed to solve this?

definitions.text: Like Holmes's face, if he'd failed to solve this?

parts.words: Like Holmes's face, if he'd failed to solve this?
parts.note: the detective would blush red with embarrassment at failing on his own first case, the title of the first Sherlock Holmes novel

explanation.surface: Sherlock Holmes would be red-faced if a case defeated him.
explanation.walkthrough: The title of Conan Doyle's first Holmes novel, read literally, describes a face studied while it glows red.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1887 novel introducing the detective has a title that also suggests a picture of a blushing face.

clue.text: A quiet river location, well chosen

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
the Po is Italy's longest river
a site is a location

explanation.surface: A quiet riverside spot that has been well chosen.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite remarks are apt and pertinent, suitably chosen.

clue.text: Holding party, ration cooked food from oven

indicators.note: keeping inside, so one piece is held within the other
cooked as in fiddled or altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party being held, the rations cooked in an oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' makes TANORI from the fodder, and 'Holding' signals that the party goes inside; a tandoor is a clay oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes baked in a clay oven of Indian origin are named after that oven.

clue.text: Plan sure to fail — late getting support of mandarin, for one

indicators.note: in a down entry, being propped up from below, so the second piece goes underneath

parts.note: the late king means the dead king
a mandarin is a kind of duck

explanation.surface: A doomed scheme, lately backed by a Chinese official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mandarin' looks like an official or an orange, but is the duck. 'getting support of' places DUCK beneath DEAD in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme with no hope of success is a hopeless case, a failure in waiting.

clue.text: Interpreted an oracle about unfortunate king

indicators.note: interpreting puts the words into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone deciphers a prophecy about a doomed monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The unfortunate king is Charles I, beheaded in 1649; the adjective means relating to a King Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: Carolean means of the reigns of Charles I or II, the former executed.

clue.text: Manoeuvre by driver needed to turn dray into yard

definitions.meaning: backing a car up, a motorist's manoeuvre

definitions.text: needed to turn dray into yard
definitions.meaning: writing the word dray backwards gives yard, a turnaround

explanation.surface: A driver must back up to get a horse-drawn cart into the yard.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing a vehicle is a manoeuvre, and reading letters backwards is a turnaround of order.

clue.text: Big girl comes up to embrace man with love

indicators.note: to hug, so the other pieces go inside
rises, so in a down entry the word is read upwards

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name
Norm is a man's name
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A big girl stands up to hug a man lovingly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes up' makes EUS in this down entry, and 'to embrace' wraps it round the man and love; love is O from the tennis score.
explanation.definitionFit: Huge, vast and enormous are all synonyms for very big.

clue.text: Writer with badge worn entered military HQ

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement, a writer in crosswords
a tag is a label or badge
clothes that are worn are on

explanation.surface: A journalist wearing a pass gets into army headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: The five-sided building in Virginia houses the US Department of Defense, the American armed forces' headquarters.

clue.text: Line study with books on this?

definitions.text: Line study with books on this?

parts.words: Line study with books on this?
parts.note: a school subject studying lines, angles and shapes, and the books written about it

explanation.surface: A pupil asks about textbooks for a course on lines.
explanation.definitionFit: The mathematical study of points, lines and shapes is the branch of maths named for earth measurement.

clue.text: Not so smart, if more self-conscious, to imbibe rum

indicators.note: to drink in, so one word takes another into its middle

parts.note: shier, a spelling of shyer, means more bashful
rum is British slang for strange, odd

explanation.surface: A bashful person drinks rum to steady nerves and ends up looking less smart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink, but it is the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabbier, of poorer quality or appearance, means less smart.

clue.text: Maintain child, concealing one's dislike

parts.note: to aver is to assert or maintain

indicators.note: hiding inside, so one piece is put within another

parts.note: a son is a child
I is the Roman numeral for one, and the 's is possessive, the one belonging to the speaker

explanation.surface: A parent supports a child while hiding a personal dislike.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong distaste or antipathy towards something is a dislike.

clue.text: Rat has to go off and hide

parts.note: milk that goes off turns sour
an animal's hide is its coat

explanation.surface: A rodent has to escape and conceal itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rat' looks like the animal, but it means a traitor, one who deserts his side.
explanation.definitionFit: A turncoat is a deserter or traitor, which is what a rat is in slang.

clue.text: Record collector gives girl a catalogue

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
a list is a catalogue

explanation.surface: A record collector gives a woman a catalogue of discs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record collector' suggests vinyl, but means one who writes annals, year-by-year records.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronicler who compiles historical records year by year is a collector of records.
